correctness.rationale: The standard boundary-enlargement reduction takes a contained triangle to a corner triangle without decreasing its inradius. For the normalized rectangle, the submitted quotient \(r=(h-xy)/P\) is correct. At any interior critical point, the second derivative in direction \((1,-1)\) is positive because \(A P''<2P\), excluding an interior maximum. The four boundary families reduce by convexity or direct differentiation to explicit one-variable values, and the long-side-base value \(h/(1+\sqrt{1+4h^2})\) dominates the other three for \(0<h\le1\). Rescaling gives the claimed formula and the midpoint-apex triangle attains it. An independent random containment check at five aspect ratios found no violation and approached the stated extremal value.
